The wrong pair is (1) Maharaja Sayajirao University – Delhi.

The chapter's list of well-known institutes and universities that offer degree and diploma courses in museology gives 'Maharaj Sayajirao University, Vadodara'. The university is in Vadodara, not Delhi; the institution the chapter lists at Delhi is the National Museum.

The other three pairs are correct: Banaras Hindu University is at Varanasi, Aligarh Muslim University at Aligarh and Jivaji University at Gwalior.

The sources of history and all the history books available today are the result of the diligent work of several historians, and institutes like libraries, museums and archives conserve and preserve this precious historical heritage.

They choose important specimens from the heritage collection and exhibit them, and they also publish research journals, informative pamphlets, leaflets and posters. The documents and artefacts that are historically very important but are not exhibited are stored after the necessary treatments for conservation and preservation, and are made available to researchers whenever necessary.

Publishing is therefore how these institutions carry what they hold beyond their own walls: it makes the knowledge in their collections available to researchers and to the general public, instead of leaving it locked in the store rooms.

Every step in this work — collecting the sources of history, creating their records and indexes, and exhibiting manuscripts, old books and artefacts after completing the necessary treatments — requires very careful handling, and a mistake at any stage can damage an irreplaceable source.

The chapter lists the training such work needs: knowledge of scripts like Brahmi, Modi and Persian and of their development; basic knowledge of the social organisation, traditions, literature and culture, dynasties and administrative systems of past societies; knowledge of the schools and styles of painting and sculptural art; knowledge of the types of paper, ink and colours; knowledge of the properties of the various stones and metals used for inscriptions; knowledge of the equipment and chemicals used in the processes of cleaning, conservation and preservation; knowledge of the approaches to managing exhibitions in museums and galleries and of information technology; and the ability to write research reports and articles.

Because the work needs all of this specialised knowledge, only trained and duly qualified persons can take up the tasks involved in conservation and preservation.

Geographic information is essential for historical studies, and a Sthalakosh is an encyclopaedia giving information about historical places.

'Sthanapothi' (14th century C.E.) is an encyclopaedic work that gives the background of the events described in 'Leelacharitra', which makes it a very good source for writing about the life of Chakradhar Swami.

'Prachin Bharatiya Sthalakosh' (1969) was compiled by Siddheshwarshstri Chitrav. It provides information about the various places mentioned in Vedic literature, the Kautiliya Arthashastra, Panini's Grammar, the Valmiki Ramayana, the Mahabharata, the Puranas, mediaeval Sanskrit literature and Shabdkosh, and also in Jain and Buddhist literature and in Greek, Chinese and Persian literature.

A Vishwakosh is a comprehensive encyclopaedia, one of the four types of encyclopaedia the chapter lists. There are two kinds of Vishwakosh: one that includes all subjects under the sun, such as 'Encyclopaedia Britannica', 'Maharashtriya Dnyankosh' and 'Marathi Vishvakosh', and one that includes comprehensive information on a single chosen subject, such as 'Bharatiya Samskruti Kosh' and 'Vyayam Dnyankosh'.

The compilation of the Marathi 'Vishwakosh' was initiated by the first Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Shri Yahswantrao Chavhan, through the Maharashtra Rajya Sahitya Samskruti Mandal, with a view to enhancing the sphere of the Marathi language and literature. The work was started under the guidance of Tarkteerth Lakshmanshastri Joshi. It contains knowledge about all possible subjects in the world, and it also contains very important entries about history.

A Samdnya Kosh is an encyclopaedic text that explains terminology.

There are such texts explaining the terminology of history — the chapter gives colonialism and globalisation as examples of the kind of term they deal with.

Because they fix the meaning of the technical vocabulary of the subject, these texts are very useful for teachers of history.

The 'Saraswati Mahal Granthalay' is in Thanjavur, Tamilnadu. It was built in the 16th-17th century, during the times of the Nayak dynasty.

In 1675 C.E. Vyankojiraje Bhosale conquered Thanjavur and established his independent rule. Vyankojiraje Bhosale and his successors kept expanding the Saraswati Mahal Granthalay, and Sarfojiraje Bhosale contributed the most to this expansion.

In 1918 the library was renamed 'The Thanjavur Maharaja Sarfoji's Saraswati Mahal Library' in his honour.

Libraries are the storehouses of knowledge and information, so how well they are managed decides whether that knowledge can actually be reached.

Library Science is very closely related to Management Science, Information Technology and the field of Education. Libraries perform various tasks: collecting books, arranging them systematically, conserving and preserving those books, and disseminating information sources. Many of these tasks are now completed with the help of computerised systems.

The most important aspect of library management is to make a book available to a reader as per his requirement — a collection that cannot be searched is of no use to the reader. The earliest libraries in the world, such as the Royal Library of Ashurbanipal in Mesopotamia, the library at Takshashila University and the library in Alexandria, show how old and how valued this work is, and India has several noteworthy libraries today, such as the National Library, Kolkata; the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library, Delhi; the State Central Library, Hyderabad; and the Library of the Asiatic Society and the David Sassoon Library in Mumbai.

From the technical point of view the management of archives is akin to library management.

The important tasks in the management of archives are preserving documents with important content in their original condition, preparing indexes, and creating accurate systems for the retrieval of documents. Documents from the archives are supposed to be very reliable, so keeping them in their original condition matters greatly. Because of the heavy dependence on computerised systems, information technology has become an inevitable part of the management of libraries and archives.

The first official archives of India, the 'Imperial Record Department', was established in 1891 C.E. in Kolkata and was shifted to Delhi in 1911 C.E. In 1998 C.E. the then President of India, K.R. Narayanan, opened the archives to the public; it is a department under the Ministry of Culture, and documents have been preserved there in chronological order from 1748, including records in English, Arabic, Hindi, Persian, Sanskrit and Urdu and in the Modi script, classified into Public records, Oriental Studies, Manuscripts and Private Records. The governments of every State in India maintain independent archives; the Archives of the Maharashtra State Government has branches in Mumbai, Pune, Kolhapur, Aurangabad and Nagpur, and the Pune branch holds about 5 crore Modi documents related to Maratha history, referred to as the 'Peshwa Daftar'.

Types of Encyclopaedia

The chapter says encyclopaedias can be approximately divided into four types, which are the four boxes of the map:

- Dictionaries
- Comprehensive Encyclopaedia (Vishwakosh)
- Encyclopaedic (Koshsadrush) literature
- Indexes

Dictionaries arrange the words of a language in a certain order, usually alphabetical, and give meanings, synonyms and etymology; there are comprehensive dictionaries, dictionaries of a certain type of word, dictionaries of terminology, etymological dictionaries, thesauruses and dictionaries of idioms and proverbs. A Vishwakosh is of two kinds — one covering all subjects, such as 'Encyclopaedia Britannica', 'Maharashtriya Dnyankosh' and 'Marathi Vishvakosh', and one covering a single chosen subject comprehensively, such as 'Bharatiya Samskruti Kosh' and 'Vyayam Dnyankosh'.
